source: Sun, Hu, Zhou, Zheng, Hajishirzi, Dziri, Song (2025) OMEGA: Can LLMs Reason Outside the Box in Math? Exploratory, Compositional, Transformative Generalization
finding: Benchmark built directly on Boden's typology: exploratory (same method, harder instances), compositional (combine two learned skills), transformative (a new tactic is needed). Frontier reasoning models lose accuracy steadily as exploratory complexity rises.
numbers: Models: DeepSeek-R1, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, o3-mini, o4-mini. Pass@k from 1 to 32 raised accuracy toward 100% at low complexity but it fell to 0 at complexity level 6 on letter-distribution problems (up to 64 attempts tested).
limits: Programmatically generated math only; the Boden mapping is the authors' analogy, not a test of human creativity.
agent_relevance: Exploratory failure is a depth/compute limit, not a missing idea: more samples do not rescue it. Do not use open-mode sampling to fix hard exploratory problems.

source: Sun et al. (2025) OMEGA, RL training experiment
finding: GRPO training on 1k problems (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) helps exploratory generalization, helps compositional only weakly, and does not help transformative generalization.
numbers: Zebra Logic: base 30%, +61 points in-distribution and +53 points OOD. Geometry: base under 15%, +31 ID, +8 OOD. Arithmetic GCD: training on levels 1-2 raised level 3 from 6% to 10%; level 5 stayed at 3%. Compositional: skills reach >69% alone, composed problems gain only about +6 in most cases, GCD+polynomial root +0. Transformative: OOD accuracy near 0% in most settings; only Setting 7 gained +10 points and trajectories still used naive solutions.
limits: 7B models, 1k training problems, RL only; the authors say transformative skill may need diverse strategies in base training or SFT.
agent_relevance: Evidence that a model will not invent a new solution paradigm on its own from reward. Transformation must be forced by the scaffold (explicit drop-a-rule step), not hoped for.

source: Sun et al. (2025) OMEGA, transformative regression case
finding: In the matrix-rank transformative setting the base model already scored well out of distribution, and RL made it worse.
numbers: Base OOD 70%; after RL a drop of 30 percentage points. In-distribution matrix rank gained +56%.
limits: One setting out of seven; the interpretation (RL entrenches brittle heuristics) is the authors' reading.
agent_relevance: Narrowing a model with repeated reward on one tactic can remove an alternative tactic it had. Keep a way back to the unnarrowed generator.

source: Sun et al. (2025) OMEGA, reasoning-trace analysis
finding: On hard Matrix Rank items DeepSeek-R1 spends less of its chain of thought on computation and more on guessing the answer.
numbers: Computation share of tokens fell from about 65% at level 1 to below 40% at level 7; conjecture statements filled the gap. Per-step arithmetic accuracy stayed high.
limits: One problem family, one model; step labels were made by o4-mini.
agent_relevance: On hard exploratory searches the model skips the search and guesses. A program that forces and counts explicit search steps (G1/G2 style) targets this.

source: Suzuki and Banaei-Kashani (2025/2026) Universe of Thoughts: A Computational Framework for Creative Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Formalizes Boden's three modes as executable LLM operators: combinational (retrieve analogue, transfer mechanism), exploratory (beam search inside the space), transformational (generate new rules/constraints that change the space, keeping immutable requirements). Compared with OnePrompt, CoT, ToT, EGoT on three new tasks and on HypoArena.
numbers: Novel tasks, GPT-4o, 10 generations per method, human creativity score (mean of novelty and utility): Bridge T-UoT 0.680 vs OnePrompt 0.480, CoT 0.590, ToT 0.580; Electricity T-UoT 0.620 vs OnePrompt 0.540, CoT 0.560, ToT 0.530; Society C-UoT 0.560 vs EGoT 0.560, OnePrompt 0.550, CoT 0.500, ToT 0.530. Human vs Gemini 2.5 Pro method-level agreement r=0.708.
limits: Small human sample per cell; scores are 0-1 means and differences on Society are tiny; no confidence intervals; preprint is on v3 dated Oct 2026.
agent_relevance: Closest published implementation of Boden's types as separate generators. It gives a rule for S3: pick the generator by task structure (see next lines).

source: Suzuki and Banaei-Kashani, UoT on HypoArena (Qwen3-14B)
finding: On 100 hypothesis tasks, Exploratory UoT ranked first among seven methods; transformational and combinational variants ranked below plain ToT and CoT.
numbers: Average Bradley-Terry rating / pairwise win rate: E-UoT 1535.4 / 32.7%; ToT 1515.8 / 25.5%; EGoT 1505.1 / 25.3%; CoT 1493.7 / 18.8%; C-UoT 1489.6 / 19.5%; T-UoT 1484.6 / 17.3%; OnePrompt 1475.7 / 14.3%. Bio 34, ML 34, Social 32 tasks; judge Gemma-3-12B.
limits: Judge is a 12B model (judge bias possible; cross-judge agreement is only moderate in the paper's Table 11); one backbone.
agent_relevance: In constrained, specific tasks the exploratory generator beat the transformational one. Default open-mode generator should be exploratory; transformation is a conditional option.

source: Suzuki and Banaei-Kashani, UoT backbone dependence and ablation
finding: The ranking flips on a weaker backbone, and mode-specific operators add only modest value over the bare search.
numbers: GLM-4-9B on the same 100 tasks: OnePrompt first (rating 1560.4, win rate 46.3%), E-UoT best structured method (1542.1, 40.7%). Operator ablation, full vs ablated win rate (chance 50%): C-UoT 58.3%, T-UoT 54.2%, E-UoT 52.4%.
limits: Ablation margins for E and T are near chance; authors say the gain is mostly search structure, not mode switching.
agent_relevance: Do not trust a mode ranking across models. Re-measure on our model; keep mode switching optional and cheap.

source: Suzuki and Banaei-Kashani, UoT cost audit
finding: Quality does not rise with tokens. The best generator was exploratory at 10x the cost of one prompt; transformational cost the most and scored lower.
numbers: Tokens per task (Qwen3-14B, 10-task subset): OnePrompt 3.7k (1.0x), CoT 3.5k, ToT 27.1k (7.4x), E-UoT 36.7k (10.0x), EGoT 101.6k (27.6x), C-UoT 134.3k (36.5x), T-UoT 193.3k (52.5x).
limits: Cost measured on 10 tasks only.
agent_relevance: Budget guard: T-UoT-style transformation costs about 5x the exploratory generator; allow it only when exploration has stalled (impasse signal).

source: Suzuki and Banaei-Kashani, UoT stage diagnosis
finding: Failure analysis: analogue retrieval almost always succeeds in C-UoT, but strong transfer of the mechanism is the weak step; in T-UoT the gate is passed 100% and the rule change is applied 75-83%.
numbers: C-UoT analogy selected 100%; strong transfer 52% on wins vs 32% on losses (Table 15). T-UoT gate passed 100%, transform applied 75% vs 83% (Table 16).
limits: Values read from text extraction of tables; small subsets of the Qwen-100 set.
agent_relevance: The weak step is applying the changed rule or transferred mechanism, which code can check; add a code-checked 'is the new rule actually used' gate.

source: Franceschelli and Musolesi (2023/2024) On the Creativity of Large Language Models
finding: Applies Boden's value/novelty/surprise and her three surprise types. Argues autoregressive LLMs at most reach combinational or exploratory creativity; transformational creativity is not reachable with current training. Adds B-novelty (new to the beholder) to explain why outputs still feel creative.
numbers: No experiment. Argument cites RLHF/DPO reducing diversity (Kirk et al. 2024).
quote: Transformational creativity is not achievable through the current LLM training solutions.
limits: Position paper; the claim concerns training, and is not contradicted by scaffolds that change rules at inference time (see c05, c20).
agent_relevance: Gives the prior: do not expect the weights to transform; if transformation happens it comes from the scaffold changing constraints.

source: Peng et al. (2025) Probing and Inducing Combinational Creativity in Vision-Language Models
finding: Combinational creativity (Boden 1998) tested as concept blending with an Identification-Explanation-Implication (IEI) scaffold on 666 artist-made visual mashups. Best VLMs beat average people at comprehension, not experts.
numbers: Implication win rate: human experts 78.3%, GPT-4o 73.5%, GPT-4V 71.9%, Gemini-1.5-Pro 71.7%, Claude-3.5-Sonnet 62.9%, average people 51.0%, LLaVA-1.5-7B 20.1%. Identification precision/recall GPT-4o 75.67/85.00 vs people 53.42/70.33.
limits: Image mashups, 2024 models; implication scored by pairwise win rate against annotations.
agent_relevance: Models can recognise a blend better than the average person but not the expert. A blend step needs an explicit 'shared attribute' stage.

source: Peng et al. (2025), IEI generation experiment
finding: Adding the explanation level (shared attributes) to the prompt improved text-to-image mashups over identification+implication only, and not because the prompt was longer.
numbers: 50 Prolific raters ranked images; Friedman p<0.0001. Midjourney mean rank IEI 1.98 vs II 2.40; win rate vs human experts 0.26 to 0.35 with IEI. Prompt length IEI M=514.53 vs II M=487.95, p=0.404; in 46.0% of IEI wins the IEI prompt was shorter. GPT-4o concepts worked in 90% (36/40) of DALLE-3 cases; 27.8% (10/36) of good descriptions failed to render.
limits: Expert artworks still ranked above all IEI outputs; Stable-Diffusion-3 gained little; execution bottleneck is the image model.
agent_relevance: A scaffold that names the shared attribute before blending lifts quality at equal length. Use a 'what do the two ideas share' slot in the combinational generator.

source: Chakrabarty, Laban, Agarwal, Muresan, Wu (2024) Art or Artifice? LLMs and the False Promise of Creativity (CHI)
finding: Torrance Test of Creative Writing (14 binary tests) with ten writers rating 48 stories. LLM stories passed 3-10 times fewer tests than professional stories. LLMs used as judges did not correlate positively with experts.
numbers: N=48 stories, 10 expert writers; 3-10X fewer tests passed; aggregate expert agreement about 0.69; LLM raters averaged correlation near zero.
limits: Short stories, 2023 models (Claude v1.3, GPT-3.5, GPT-4); not specific to Boden types.
agent_relevance: Supports G5: no model judge on creativity. Select with code (diversity, constraint checks), not model-rated creativity.

source: Gomez-Rodriguez and Williams (2023) A Confederacy of Models: a Comprehensive Evaluation of LLMs on Creative Writing
finding: One hard prompt (a fight between a novel's hero and a pterosaur). Top commercial models roughly matched or slightly beat human writers on most criteria, open models fell behind, humans stayed ahead on creativity.
numbers: Abstract has no figures; human judges rated fluency, coherence, originality, humor, style.
limits: Abstract page opened, full text not read; single prompt.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence; useful only as contrast: exploratory polish is easy, originality is the gap.

source: Mohammadi (2024) Creativity Has Left the Chat: The Price of Debiasing Language Models
finding: Compared Llama-2 base vs RLHF-aligned models: aligned models showed less syntactic and semantic diversity in persona and review generation, so the space they explore shrinks.
numbers: Three experiments on the Llama-2 series (exact scores not recovered from the text extraction).
limits: Digits were lost in PDF text extraction, so no figures are recorded; diversity here is lexical/semantic, not Boden-valued creativity.
agent_relevance: Alignment narrows the explorable space; for open mode use diversity-recovering prompt formats (c19) and a novelty memory.

source: Matthews and Hamilton (2026) Language Models are Lazy Poets: Creative Mode Collapse at Scale
finding: 1.1 million poems from 16 open-weight models over 15 forms and 248 topics. Aggregate output is collapsed onto a few words, openings and rhymes, but a large latent inventory exists in the long tail.
numbers: Top 1% of rhyming pairs cover 30.7% (Qwen3 30B-A3B) to 49.8% (Gemma 3 4B) of rhyme occurrences; top 1% of content words cover 46.3% to 61.5%. Model size vs distinct rhyme words r=0.719-0.765 (p<0.002). Ministral 3B uses 'light' in 65% of poems. Human reference: 1,442 Poetry Foundation poems (unbalanced).
limits: Open-weight models only; poetry only; human baseline small and not matched.
agent_relevance: Direct size of the exploratory space: the model can reach far more than it usually does. Open mode needs forced exclusion of modal outputs (novelty memory), which code can do.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
finding: Blind review by 79 experts: an LLM agent with retrieval, over-generate and rerank produced ideas rated more novel than human expert ideas, with a possible small cost in feasibility.
numbers: 49 ideas per condition. Novelty mean: human 4.84, AI 5.64 (p<0.01), AI + human rerank 5.81 (p<0.001). Reviewer agreement 56.1% vs 66.0% for NeurIPS 2021. LLM judges on pairwise ranking: GPT-4o 61.1%, Claude-3-Opus 63.5%.
limits: Ideas not executed; reviewer agreement is low; NLP prompting-topic ideas only.
agent_relevance: Over-generate and rank can beat humans on rated novelty, but see c18: the pool saturates.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024), diversity limit of idea generation
finding: The exploratory pool saturates: scaling generation just repeats ideas.
numbers: Of 4000 generated seed ideas per topic only 200 were non-duplicates (cosine similarity above 0.8 with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 counted as duplicate); the non-duplicate share per batch kept falling and the accumulated total plateaued.
limits: Single agent pipeline and single embedding model; the 0.8 threshold is a choice.
agent_relevance: A code-run duplicate filter plus a plateau signal is a measurable stall detector: when the new-idea rate drops, switch from the exploratory to a rule-changing generator.

source: Zhang, Yu, Chong, Sicilia, Tomz, Manning, Shi (2026, ICML) Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
finding: Training-free prompt: ask for several responses with probabilities. Raises diversity without loss of quality; cause traced to typicality bias in preference data.
numbers: Creative writing diversity up 1.6-2.1x over direct prompting; larger models gain 1.5-2x more than small ones (GPT-4.1, Gemini-2.5-Pro vs mini/flash); Tulu-70B base diversity 45.4% while direct prompting falls after SFT/DPO and VS stays higher; diversity tunable by a probability threshold in the prompt.
limits: Plain VS lowers quality slightly on small models; VS-CoT and VS-Multi avoid this on large models.
agent_relevance: A cheap exploratory-space widener for S3: one call, several candidates with stated probabilities, then code picks low-probability ones. Probabilities are only an ordering hint, not a judgment.

source: Lu, Wang, Li, Jiang, Khudanpur, Jiang, Khashabi (2025, NAACL) Benchmarking Language Model Creativity: A Case Study on Code Generation (Denial Prompting, NeoGauge)
finding: Denial Prompting forbids the previous solution's technique (e.g. no for loops) step by step. This is a rule-dropping, transformational-style operator with unit-test checking. 199 Codeforces problems, 30 human solutions each.
numbers: GPT-4 had the highest NeoGauge at almost every step; Claude-3 and Llama3-70B matched GPT-4 at step 0 but fell to 0 within two steps. Of four reasoning strategies (MCTS, self-correction, planning, sampling), only MCTS raised divergent creativity and its NeoGauge gain was 0 after step 2; sampling divergent difference was -1.2 at t=0 and t=3.
limits: Code with checkable constraints; constraints are imposed by the experimenter, not discovered by the model.
agent_relevance: A checkable constraint-denial loop is a concrete transformation operator: output must pass tests AND avoid the banned technique. Code can verify both.

source: Lehman, Gordon, Jain, Ndousse, Yeh, Stanley (2022) Evolution through Large Models
finding: LLM as mutation operator inside MAP-Elites quality-diversity search. Produced hundreds of thousands of working Sodarace walker programs in a domain absent from pretraining, then bootstrapped a conditional model.
numbers: Map of 1,728 niches; nearly all seeds fill the map (Square seed slower); fine-tuning the diff model on accepted diffs raised niches reached and QD score (Figures 8-11).
limits: Toy domain; compute heavy; requires a fitness evaluator and behaviour descriptors.
agent_relevance: An exploratory engine over a grid of behaviour cells with code-run fitness, no model judge. Good fit for S3 when niches can be defined by code.

source: Novikov et al. (2025) AlphaEvolve: a coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
finding: LLM-driven evolutionary loop with automatic evaluators. On more than 50 open math problems it matched the best known construction on 75% and found better constructions on 20%.
numbers: Tensor decomposition: 54 targets, matched state of the art in 38, surpassed in 14, fell behind in 2. Kissing number in dimension 11 raised to 593.
limits: Needs an automatic scorer; works where verifying is cheap; vendor-reported.
agent_relevance: Strongest evidence that 'exploratory search plus code verifier' yields real novelty. Reuse the pattern for any task with a checker.

source: Boden (1990/2004) The Creative Mind: Myths and Mechanisms
finding: Source of the three types: combinational, exploratory, transformational; P-creativity vs H-creativity. The book was not read; only the Wikipedia page was checked.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Wikipedia confirms exploratory vs transformational and P/H-creativity only; it does not describe combinational or conceptual spaces. Boden text NOT opened.
agent_relevance: Definition only: transformation means changing the rules that define the space.

source: Wiggins (2006) Searching for computational creativity; A preliminary framework for description, analysis and comparison of creative systems
finding: Formal version of Boden: a conceptual space defined by rules R, a traversal strategy T and an evaluation E over a universe U; exploratory creativity moves with T inside the R-defined space, transformational creativity changes R (or T/E). Recalled from memory; the Wikipedia page names Wiggins only in passing.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Not opened as a primary source. Treat details of R, T, E as unverified.
agent_relevance: Code-friendly spec: R = checkable constraints, T = generator strategy, E = code scorer. Transformation = edit R, T or E explicitly.

source: Ritchie (2007) Some empirical criteria for attributing creativity to a computer program
finding: Proposed measurable criteria on output sets (typicality, quality, novelty). Recalled, not opened this session.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Memory only; verify before citing.
agent_relevance: Typicality vs quality sets could be coded as selection filters.
